network: ctx.serve(cert/lib/fake-aws.mjs) behind the kernel's realm proxy (https_proxy 127.0.0.1:3128): a fake of STS, S3 (and an S3 multi-region access point, SigV4a only), SSO OIDC, the SSO portal, EC2, EC2 Instance Connect, CloudTrail and AWS Sign-In on their real hostnames; wasm-tls-engine lets the proxy terminate CONNECT with the kernel CA, which botocore verifies through AWS_CA_BUNDLE (the launcher's default, SSL_CERT_FILE). The fake logs every request, and the specs check the log in Node: SigV4 and SigV4a signatures, DPoP proofs and CRCs with Node's own code (cert/lib/sigv4.mjs, cert/lib/crc.mjs)

patches.awscrt-optional.patch: awscrt is optional, as in standalone botocore (botocore.compat.HAS_CRT, False with homescoop's crypto-only awscrt), with pure-Python CRC32C, CRC64NVME and CRC combining (botocore/crc.py), the classic S3 transfer client, and SigV4a on cryptography (botocore/sigv4a.py). Without it every command fails with No module named 'awscrt' (NEGATIVE.md). version.mjs (HAS_CRT False, the awscrt in the tree is src/awscrt and nothing else), checksums.mjs (botocore.crc against Node, the checksum classes, the CRC32 default), s3.mjs (CRC32C/CRC64NVME uploads, validated downloads, the combined full-object CRC64NVME of a ranged download, the classic multipart client, XXHASH64 refused), sts.mjs (no md/awscrt in the user agent), sigv4a.mjs (aws-c-auth's SigV4a suite and a multi-region access point end to end; without the AUTH_TYPE_MAPS hunk: Unknown Signature Version: v4a, NEGATIVE.md), ec2-password.mjs (a missing cryptography is not reported as a bad key), crt-only.mjs (open-tunnel says it needs awscrt, rc 255, sends nothing; preferred_transfer_client = crt warns; the commands' help renders), launcher.mjs (a fake awscrt in site-packages is not picked up)
patches.help-text.patch: version.mjs: aws help and aws s3 cp help render as text with no groff or mandoc on PATH; without it they fail with Could not find executable named "groff or mandoc" (NEGATIVE.md)
patches.login-remote.patch: login.mjs: aws login takes the cross-device flow (--remote) with no flag: it prints the authorize URL and reads the code; without it, it starts the same-device flow with a callback server on 127.0.0.1 and waits for a redirect no browser in slicc can deliver (NEGATIVE.md)
patches.sso-device-code.patch: sso.mjs: aws sso login takes the device code flow with no flag; without it, it starts the Authorization Code flow with a callback server on 127.0.0.1 and waits for a redirect no browser in slicc can deliver (NEGATIVE.md)

notices.name: docutils
notices.text: Most of the files included in this project have been placed in the public domain

checklist: cert/version.mjs: aws --version is aws-cli/<homescoop.upstream> Python/3.15.x, nothing on stderr; in wasix-python, the only awscrt is lib/aws-cli/awscrt (homescoop's crypto-only one: no _awscrt, awscrt.auth, awscrt.s3 or awscrt.checksums) and botocore.compat.HAS_CRT is False; aws help and aws s3 cp help print text (Description, the synopsis, "--checksum-algorithm" (string), Examples) with no groff or mandoc; aws_completer completes 'aws s3 c', 'aws sts get-caller-i' and '--instance-i' from the generated ac.index

cert/sts.mjs: aws sts get-caller-identity over https through the kernel proxy returns the fake's identity; the one request is POST https://sts.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ with Action=GetCallerIdentity, its SigV4 signature verified in Node with the secret key, no md/awscrt in the user agent; --query Account --output text, --output yaml (exactly) and table; --region eu-west-1 goes to sts.eu-west-1; keys written by aws configure set to ~/.aws/credentials sign the call; AccessDenied is rc 254 with the CLI's message; no credentials is rc 253 'Unable to locate credentials'

cert/s3.mjs: aws s3 ls; aws s3 cp up sends aws-chunked with a CRC32 trailer equal to Node's CRC32, SigV4 verified; s3api put-object --checksum-algorithm CRC32C and CRC64NVME send Node's values (pure Python); XXHASH64 is rc 255 'Missing Dependency: … requires awscrt'; aws s3 cp down asks for the checksum (x-amz-checksum-mode ENABLED), validates the object's CRC64NVME and gets the bytes, and a wrong checksum is rc 1 'did not match calculated checksum'; with 5 MB multipart settings an 11 MiB + 1 upload is CreateMultipartUpload, 3 UploadParts each with Node's CRC32 of its slice, CompleteMultipartUpload; a 6 MiB + 3 CRC64NVME object downloads in 2 ranged GETs whose combined checksum is validated (--debug 'Full object crc64nvme checksum validated'), and a wrong one fails

cert/checksums.mjs: in wasix-python, botocore.crc gives the CRC-32C and CRC-64/NVME check values, and on 70001 + 130003 random bytes the same CRC32, CRC32C and CRC64NVME as Node (cert/lib/crc.mjs), chained and through combine_*; s3transfer's combine functions are botocore.crc's; botocore's checksum classes are crc32, crc32c, crc64nvme, sha1, sha256 and sha512 (no xxhash), the crc64nvme class matches Node, the default request checksum is CRC32 and HAS_CRT is False

cert/sso.mjs: with a profile on an sso-session, aws sso login (no flag, --use-device-code, --no-browser) on a pty prints the device verification URL and code, polls CreateToken past one authorization_pending, says 'Successfully logged into Start URL', caches the token in ~/.aws/sso/cache, and names no 127.0.0.1, localhost or oauth/callback; its requests are RegisterClient, StartDeviceAuthorization (the start URL), CreateToken twice; aws sts get-caller-identity --profile cert then gets role credentials from the SSO portal with the bearer token (account, role) and signs STS with them (session token sent, SigV4 verified)

cert/launcher.mjs: a .pth, a jmespath that raises and a fake awscrt in wasix-python's site-packages, all seen by a plain python3, are ignored by aws (python3 -S) and by python3 bin/aws (site-packages dropped); bin/aws's sys.path is lib/aws-cli first, then the standard library, then exactly py-cffi's and py-cryptography's site-packages (the versions package.json pins; cryptography and _cffi_backend load from them), and no other node_modules directory: a py-* package that a plain python3 discovers (its jmespath raises) is not on it, and with py-cffi at another version found first (a copy in aws-cli/node_modules) it is refused and cloudfront sign says 'Missing Dependency: This command needs cryptography' (No module named '_cffi_backend'), rc 255, no traceback; without SSL_CERT_FILE botocore's own bundle fails with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED, AWS_CA_BUNDLE set to the kernel CA works, a user's AWS_CA_BUNDLE wins over the default; on a pty there is no pager by default, and AWS_PAGER='tee <file>' gets the output; the launcher under another name exits 1

cert/crt-only.mjs: ec2-instance-connect open-tunnel exits 255 with 'Missing Dependency: EC2 Instance Connect's websocket tunnel requires awscrt, the AWS Common Runtime, which this AWS CLI build does not include.', no traceback and no request sent; with preferred_transfer_client = crt, aws s3 cp warns that it needs awscrt and uses the classic client; aws login help, cloudfront sign help, cloudtrail validate-logs help, ec2-instance-connect open-tunnel and ssh help and ec2 get-password-data help render

cert/cloudfront.mjs: the AWS CLI's 30 cross-SDK CloudFront cases (tests/functional/cloudfront/testdata), run as upstream's test_sign_shared_cases.py runs them, in one python through bin/aws's setup and the CLI's entry point (lib/aws_many.py), three of them also as aws commands with the same result: 13 signed URLs and 5 signed cookies with the expected parameters and policy, every RSA-SHA1 and RSA-SHA256 signature (PKCS#1 and PKCS#8 keys) byte for byte the expected one, every signature (ECDSA P-256 too, PKCS#8 and SEC1) verified in Node with the test key's public key; 12 error cases (ECDSA with SHA-1, a DSA key, JSON injection, missing or inverted dates) with their rc and message and no traceback

cert/ec2-password.mjs: get-password-data --priv-launch-key with the AWS CLI's own test blob (test_get_password_data.py) and testcli.pem, as PKCS#1 and as PKCS#8 (converted by Node), prints PasswordData "=mG8.r$o-s"; without the flag the blob is printed; another RSA key and a file that isn't a key are "Unable to decrypt password data using provided private key file.", rc 255, no traceback

cert/cloudtrail.mjs: verify-query-results on the AWS CLI's CloudTrail Lake export, signed by CloudTrail (result_sign.json, result_1.csv.gz, the key with fingerprint 67b9fa73… from ListPublicKeys), from a local directory and from S3: 'Successfully validated sign and query result files'; a changed export file is 'inconsistent hash value', a changed signature 'Invalid signature in sign file', a key that isn't PKCS#1 DER 'unable to load PKCS #1 key', rc != 0, no traceback; validate-logs --verbose on two chained digest files and their logs (gzip, signature in x-amz-meta-signature), built and signed in Node with the CLI's CloudTrail test key: both digests and both logs valid, rc 0; a changed log 'INVALID: hash value doesn't match' and a changed digest signature 'INVALID: signature verification failed', rc 1

cert/eic.mjs: ec2-instance-connect ssh --connection-type direct (DescribeInstances: a public IP) with a fake ssh on PATH: SendSSHPublicKey gets ssh-ed25519 <key> for ec2-user, ssh gets -p 22 -i <key file> ec2-user@203.0.113.10 and aws exits with ssh's status (7); the key file is an unencrypted openssh-key-v1 Ed25519 key, parsed in Node (ciphers none, check numbers, padding), whose public key is the one pushed and which signs what it verifies; a second run makes a new key

cert/login.mjs: aws login --profile cert-login --region us-east-1, answered by a driver that pastes base64(code=…&state=<the URL's state>) at the prompt: the cross-device flow with no flag (no 127.0.0.1), the token request is grantType authorization_code for arn:aws:signin:::devtools/cross-device with a code verifier matching the URL's S256 challenge and an ES256 DPoP proof (dpop+jwt, htm POST, htu the token URL, iat, jti) that verifies in Node with its own jwk; the token cache has that key as a SEC1 EC PRIVATE KEY PEM and the profile login_session; the next sts get-caller-identity refreshes the soon-expiring token (grantType refresh_token) with a DPoP proof from the reloaded key (the same jwk), and signs STS with the new credentials and session token (SigV4 verified); the call after that does not refresh

cert/sigv4a.mjs: aws-c-auth's SigV4a test suite (fixtures/sigv4a-suite.json) signed with botocore/sigv4a.py in the kernel (lib/sigv4a_suite.py, through bin/aws's setup): for 30 tests the derived key is the suite's public key (and Node's own derivation), the canonical request and string to sign are the suite's, the Authorization header is the suite's but for the signature, which verifies in Node, and the suite's own signature verifies with the same key; for 27 of them the same for the presigned URL; the tests botocore has no signer for are listed with the reason; an S3 multi-region access point (arn:aws:s3::123456789012:accesspoint/mfzwi23gnjvgw.mrap): get-object and put-object go to <alias>.mrap.accesspoint.s3-global.amazonaws.com signed with SigV4a (region set *, service s3, x-amz-region-set signed) as Node verifies with the key it derives, and aws s3 presign gives a SigV4a URL (X-Amz-Region-Set *, X-Amz-Expires 600) that the fake serves and Node verifies

cert/notices.mjs: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md has colorama, distro, docutils, jmespath, prompt_toolkit, python-dateutil, ruamel.yaml, six, urllib3 and wcwidth with their licenses' text; LICENSE is AWS's notice followed by the Apache License 2.0

test/files.test.mjs (host, the test job): lib/aws-cli/awscli is the recipe's release with the four patches applied, lib/aws-cli/awscrt is src/awscrt and nothing else, no __pycache__, .pyc, native code or links, the wheels' .data and RECORD files left out; every lock dependency but awscrt and ruamel.yaml.clib is there at the lock's version; ac.index is an SQLite database; bin/aws and bin/aws_completer are src/launcher.py, mode 0755, and the only slicc.commands; package.json pins py-cryptography and py-cffi exactly
test/crc.test.mjs (host): botocore/crc.py from the package, run by the runner's python3, against Node's CRCs on random data, chained and combined
by hand, not in CI (no AWS credentials in CI): nothing yet against real AWS; the fakes reproduce the wire shapes of STS, S3, SSO OIDC and the SSO portal
fixtures: cert/fixtures (written by cert/fixtures/fetch.mjs, by hand): aws-c-auth's SigV4a test suite at a pinned commit (sigv4a-suite.json), and the AWS CLI's own functional test data from the recipe's source distribution: CloudFront's cross-SDK signing cases and keys (cloudfront/), the Windows password blob and key of test_get_password_data.py (ec2/), a CloudTrail Lake export signed by CloudTrail and its key, and the CLI's CloudTrail test key (cloudtrail/); Apache-2.0
